note: HEBREW RECOVERY, not a defect repair — Corpus Corporum's TEI dropped the Hebrew type Migne sets inline, leaving the documented scar (a DOUBLED SPACE where the glyphs stood). Method: hebrew-recovery.md. Read from the on-disk PL 113 scan, archive.org patrologiaecurs04migngoog (raw/scans/pl113/), PDF page = (column + 11) / 2 — re-derived off the printed corner numbers at chunking and in agreement with 8944's map on the same scan; the volume itself was confirmed from the plate (PATROL. CXIII. at the foot of p. 426) rather than from the archive id, whose '04' is the item number. Rendered full page width at 150 dpi, then a region crop at 600 dpi. Recorded as a TEI patch rather than a chunk edit so a re-chunk reproduces it — a chunk-level insertion is erased silently by the next chunk run. Provenance: data/hebrew-patches/8967.json.
class: FOUND BY THE CHUNKING PLATE SPOT CHECK, on the work's own opening page — the page the check was already required to read, and the same way 8944's three sites were found. ⚑ THE ORDER IS THE MIRROR OF 8944's: there Migne sets the Hebrew BEFORE his transliteration, here he sets the transliteration first and the Hebrew after it in PARENTHESES ('nebel (נבל)'). The parentheses are Migne's and are kept. Confirmed three ways: the doubled-space scar in the TEI, the glyphs on the plate at 600 dpi, and Migne's own transliteration printed beside them — nothing is inferred from the Latin alone. ⚠ ZERO Hebrew codepoints survive anywhere in this work's 96,650-word TEI, so CC's drop is total rather than selective; that is the reason a scar sweep was run at all.

patches.find: <hi>nebel</hi>  , apud Graecos,
patches.replace: <hi>nebel</hi> <foreign xml:lang="hebrew">(נבל),</foreign> apud Graecos,
patches.why: Migne prints 'Psalterium apud Hebraeos vocatur nebel (נבל), apud Graecos ψαλτήριον, apud Latinos vero organum.' The TEI kept the transliteration and the Greek and dropped only the Hebrew, leaving a DOUBLED SPACE before the comma — the scar hebrew-recovery.md step 1 describes. Three consonants nun-bet-lamed, read directly off the plate at 600 dpi and unambiguous. NOT a scriptural quotation but the common noun נבל (harp/lyre), so the MT check of step 5 is replaced by Migne's own three-language gloss in the same clause: nebel / ψαλτήριον / organum. Migne's type here shows no vowel points at this copy's resolution and none are supplied — the consonants are read, the pointing is not asserted. ⚑ The parentheses AND the trailing comma sit INSIDE the <foreign> element, which looks odd but is the source's own convention: CC encodes the Greek in this very clause as '<foreign xml:lang="greek">ψαλτήριον,</foreign>', comma included. The reason is mechanical — the chunker strips an unrecognized tag by replacing it with whitespace, so anything left outside comes through as '( נבל ) ,' with spaces Migne does not print, and a stray space before a comma is the very scar this patch exists to remove. Leaving one here would plant a false positive for the next scar sweep. 8944 never met this case: its Hebrew stands beside no punctuation. ⚑ Band corrected 2026-09-04: filed as 0841C, but the find resolves inside 0841B — which is also the column the pending-patch file and data/hebrew-patches/8967.json both record for this recovery. The three sources now agree.

patches.why: TWO defects at one site, both CC's encoding rather than Migne's type, and both would have reached the reader. (1) An EMPTY <hi></hi> element: it carries no text, and the chunker renders it as a bare '**' standing in the running prose. (2) The note's content is '([Num. XVI] \n)' — Migne does print this reference in SQUARE brackets inside his parenthesis, so CC is being faithful, but our note syntax OWNS square brackets and the chunker normalizes an interior '[ ]' to '( )'. The two combine to '**[n: ((Num. XVI) )]' — doubled parens plus a stray space from the newline. Rendered as '[n: (Num. XVI)]', which is exactly how this work prints its other 3,375 references. NOT a silent emendation of Migne: his bracket-vs-paren variation for a bare scripture reference carries no sense our apparatus can lose, and the reference itself is untouched.

unread: The scar sweep across all 106 chunks found 13 stray-space candidates; only this one was read at the plate. The other 12 are NOT claimed as drops — a stray space has ordinary causes too, and hebrew-recovery.md step 1 makes the scan the arbiter, not the scar. Three 'In Hebraeo' clauses also stand in this work, none with surviving Hebrew, and all three are unread candidates. Exposure here is small by the standards of an etymological work; it was worth a sweep and is not worth a campaign.
countNote: ⚑ THESE TWO SITES ARE ALSO WHY THE MASTER BRIEF'S TOTALS LINE READ 5999 WHILE THE FILE HELD 5997 SPANS. Each empty <hi></hi> was collected as a span and then dropped at print time, so the headline counted rows the file does not contain. The runbook makes that total load-bearing — stints are told to count their own Latin against it — so a stint would have hunted two spans that never existed. Removing the empty elements reconciles it; lemma-inventory.mjs was also fixed to total what it prints.
bandA_pass: 39 patches applied in ONE pass 2026-09-04, after Band A's translation was complete and before the cruces merge, so that no patch rewrote Latin under a stint that was still writing. Sources: the eight Band A cruces files, each site read at the plate by the stint that reported it. ⛔ TWO REPORTED SITES WERE DELIBERATELY NOT APPLIED. (1) `locutus egomet` -> `locutos`: at 900 dpi the glyph is ambiguous, and `locutus` (perfect deponent, 'and afterwards I myself spoke') is correct Latin where `locutos` is a solecism -- a patch needs positive evidence, and applying this would have corrupted good Latin into an error. (2) `possit` -> `rossit` and the like: THE PLATE'S BROKEN SORTS ARE NOT MIGNE'S ERRORS. A damaged `p` that images as `r` is the condition of THIS COPY's inking, not a reading of the edition; restoring it would import a defect that exists nowhere but in one physical leaf. Compositor errors (wrong sorts SET) are restored; ink damage is not. That line is new and is the reason `iniquitetem` and `Nocere` ARE restored while `rossit` is not. (3) `Desiderabilia` -> `Desiderabillia` deferred: two occurrences stand in col 0871D and the report does not say which, so the leaf must be re-read rather than guessed.
patchAudit: scripts/patch-audit.mjs, added 2026-09-04: resolves every find's offset to its enclosing <pb/> and compares with the declared col, refuses a no-op replace, and warns where a patched column has no recorded plate read. chunk-work.mjs checks UNIQUENESS only, and uniqueness is not location — a find can match exactly once in the wrong column, leaving the real defect and corrupting a column nobody collated (9003, 2026-08-28). Run on Band A's 43 it found 1 mis-recorded column and 24 patches filed with NO column at all, so the check had never been possible on more than half the file. All now resolved from the TEI itself.
